title: Severity-tiered hotpatch orchestration and safe backport playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We lack a single canonical playbook that maps severity tiers to concrete branch strategies, backport windows, rollout gates, and automated tooling actions. Recent incidents (INC-2026-03-A and postmortem notes linked below) showed inconsistent backport decisions and slow rollouts when a patch needed LTS propagation. This ticket codifies a severity-driven orchestration model and implements a standardized, minimal-risk hotpatch+rollback workflow for runtime and console releases.

Scope: Define severity levels, branch naming and backport matrix for stable/LTS channels, gating checks (monitoring, canary metrics, traffic shift), and a set of scripts/CI job templates that create patch branches and apply backports with safety checks. Not in scope: implementation of a new CI provider or changing LTS cadence.

Goals:
- Create an unambiguous severity matrix that maps incident class -> allowed target channels (stable, lts, edge) and SLA windows for backports.
- Standardize branch and tag conventions for hotpatches and backports so automation and oncall can reconcile commits quickly.
- Implement gating checklist and minimal automated rollback triggers tied to telemetry (error budget, latency p95, rate of 5xx).
- Provide runbook copy and a set of GitHub Action/CI job templates to create, test, and merge patch branches into target channels with signed approvals.

Proposed severity matrix (summary):
- Sev 0 (Critical security or data-loss): Immediate hotpatch allowed across all active channels. Patch branches: patch/sev0/<short-description>. Backports: immediate to current stable and all supported LTS branches within 48 hours. Rollout gating: automated canary to 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15-minute observation windows and automated rollback on breach of error budget.
- Sev 1 (Production impacting, high customer-visibility): Hotpatch to stable and newest LTS only. Backports: target LTS within 7 days. Manual approval required from Release Lead + Oncall.
- Sev 2 (Degraded feature or degraded perf): Targeted fix to stable; LTS backport evaluated case-by-case. Backport window: 14 days if customer requests.
- Sev 3 (Low impact, cosmetic): No hotpatch; include in next minor release.

Branch naming conventions:
- patch/sev{N}/{area}/{short-desc}  e.g., patch/sev0/runtime-kvcache-nullptr
- backport/{target-branch}/patch-{original-pr-number}
- emergency-main-merge for one-off merges that require fast reconciliation in main prior to normal release cycles

Backport matrix (examples):
- runtime-1.20 (current stable) <- receive Sev0/Sev1/Sev2 as defined
- lts-2025.10 <- receive Sev0 and curated Sev1 backports only
- lts-2023.04 (EOL) <- no backports unless security with exec signoff

Gating checks and automated rollback triggers (implementation notes):
- Canary monitoring job will evaluate p95 latency, 5xx ratio, error budget consumption, and anomalous increase in dropped requests. Thresholds are defined per service and loaded from SSM/Config.
- If any metric crosses the configured threshold during a canary window, CI automation annotates the patch PR and triggers the rollback playflow (auto-deployment of previous image and tagging).
- Rollback criteria include: sustained p95 increase > 30% for 10m, 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase, or violation of error budget.

Operational controls and approvals:
- Sev0 flow: Oncall may request immediate deploy. Post-deploy, conduct 48-hour postmortem running with stakeholders.
- Severities requiring human approvals will use the release-team Slack channel + a GitHub PR approval checklist.
- All security-sensitive patches must route through Security Review; automated gating blocks merge until security signoff label applied.

Deliverables:
1) Playbook doc (Confluence link): step-by-step hotpatch + rollback flow and severity decision tree.
2) CI templates: create-patch-branch, run-backport-tests, canary-deploy, rollback-on-failure.
3) Smallish helper CLI (python) to create branch names and open prefilled PR templates with metadata.
4) Example run against a recent incident as a dry-run to validate timings.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Broad automatic backporting reduces human error but increases merge conflicts and maintenance cost; mitigate by restricting automated backports to Sev0 and only the last two LTS branches.
- Rapid rollouts reduce customer blast radius but add complexity to monitoring thresholds. We'll default to conservative thresholds and require manual escalation for non-Sev0 flows.

Signal integrations and links:
- Incident postmortem: https://confluence.internal.redwood/INC-2026-03-A-postmortem
- Example PR pattern: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2416
- Temporary runbook draft: https://confluence.internal.redwood/release-infra/hotpatch-playbook-draft
- Monitoring dashboard template: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/patch-canary/patch-canary-summary

Next steps:
- Finalize severity rubric with Release Lead and Security by 2026-03-08.
- Implement CI job templates and CLI helper (work split).
- Run a dry-run on an old non-production bug to validate timings and rollback automation.

Notes on LTS policy alignment: This playbook is intentionally prescriptive for supported LTSes only. Where LTS policy allows patches, we will publish an LTS backport calendar and a maintainer schedule.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook doc published and linked in the release-infra playbook space; 2) CI templates merged in runtime/.github/workflows and tested in a dry-run; 3) Helper CLI PR merged; 4) Oncall dry-run completed with telemetry validating automated rollback triggers; 5) Release Lead and Security have reviewed and signed off.
